paragraphs: This paper studies how to recover a hidden ordering of items from noisy measurements of their pairwise similarity. Its central assumption is that similarity reflects position: items near one another in the underlying order tend to be more similar than items farther apart. The task is therefore to reconstruct a sequence from indirect, imperfect evidence about which items belong near each other.

The setting is active, meaning the learner chooses which pair to measure next. It does not simply receive a fixed collection of observations. This makes measurement selection part of the problem: the algorithm must gather enough useful information to identify the ordering while controlling the number of queries it uses.

The proposed algorithm comes with a high-probability guarantee of recovering the correct order. The authors also establish optimal guarantees for both error probability and observation requirements. These are statistical claims under the stated ordering-and-similarity setting; recovery is highly probable rather than certain. The contribution connects reliable reconstruction with efficient, sequential evidence collection.
neurips-2025-active-seriation-efficient-.tldr: An active algorithm recovers hidden item orderings from noisy similarity queries with optimal statistical guarantees.

paragraphs: AtmosSci-Bench provides a structured way to evaluate language models on atmospheric science problems. It covers hydrology, atmospheric dynamics, atmospheric physics, geophysics, and physical oceanography. The motivation is that applying models to scientific work requires a domain-specific assessment of their reasoning and problem solving, beyond general impressions of language fluency.

The benchmark combines multiple-choice and open-ended questions. Multiple-choice questions support automated evaluation at scale, while open-ended responses allow closer examination of conceptual understanding and reasoning. A template-based process creates graduate-level multiple-choice problems using symbolic perturbations, producing variations within the problem-generation framework. The two formats therefore examine complementary aspects of model capability.

The authors evaluate instruction-tuned, advanced reasoning, math-augmented, and climate-specific models. This comparison is designed to examine how different kinds of model development translate into atmospheric science performance. The abstract reports insights from the evaluation without identifying a winning group or specific performance gaps. The stated contribution is a common, rigorous evaluation framework that could support further development of language-model applications in climate services.
neurips-2025-atmossci-bench-evaluating-t.tldr: AtmosSci-Bench evaluates language-model reasoning across five atmospheric science fields using multiple-choice and open-ended problems.

paragraphs: In-context learning lets a language model learn from labeled examples placed in its prompt, but its behavior can become unstable as more demonstrations lengthen that prompt. This paper treats those demonstrations as a source of training signals that can be transferred into a small adapter. The aim is to separate the influence of demonstrations from the information carried by the query itself.

An in-context learning teacher first produces labels for unlabeled queries. A student then learns to predict those labels while seeing only each query, updating a lightweight adapter rather than relying on the full demonstration prompt. This stores demonstration effects in a compact, reusable form. The resulting model can still be combined with new demonstrations.

Although the teacher's labels contain errors, the student often performs better than the teacher. The authors connect this to correcting pseudo-labels and expanding coverage, consistent with weak-to-strong generalization. Experiments report better generalization, stability, and efficiency on both in-domain and out-of-domain tasks, exceeding standard in-context learning and earlier disentanglement methods.
neurips-2025-disentangling-latent-shifts.tldr: A lightweight student adapter absorbs demonstration effects from an in-context teacher, improving efficiency and often surpassing its noisy teacher.

paragraphs: DP-LLM addresses how an on-device language model should adapt when queries come with different latency and accuracy requirements. Multi-scale quantization makes runtime adaptation possible by overlaying model variants that use different numerical bitwidths. The remaining challenge is choosing a configuration that provides a useful balance between model performance and the time needed to generate an answer.

The paper's key observation is that a layer's sensitivity to numerical precision changes across decoding steps. A precision allocation that suits one stage of generation may therefore be less suitable at another. DP-LLM uses input values to assign precision dynamically to individual layers, extending the idea of mixed precision into a decision that changes during generation.

Experiments across multiple models and benchmarks report a better performance-latency trade-off than prior approaches. The finding supports using the current computation to guide precision allocation rather than treating layer sensitivity as fixed throughout decoding. Its practical significance is more adaptable use of the available precision choices when serving language models under runtime constraints.
neurips-2025-dp-llm-runtime-model-adapta.tldr: DP-LLM dynamically adjusts each layer's numerical precision during decoding to improve the performance-latency trade-off.

paragraphs: EvoBrain models EEG recordings as an evolving network for seizure detection. The paper identifies a mismatch in methods that process changing signals while keeping their graph connections fixed: brain connectivity itself evolves during seizure progression. It also examines how temporal signal processing and graph structure should interact to represent seizure and non-seizure states.

The authors provide theoretical analysis establishing an expressivity advantage for explicitly dynamic modeling and a time-then-graph approach. Their model combines a two-stream Mamba architecture with a graph convolutional network enhanced by Laplacian positional encoding. Both graph nodes and edges can change over time, allowing the representation to reflect changing connectivity as well as changing signals.

Compared with a dynamic GNN baseline, the abstract reports improvements of 23% in AUROC and 30% in F1 score. The authors also evaluate the method on early seizure prediction. Together, the theoretical and empirical results support explicitly representing network evolution in this setting, rather than expecting temporal signal processing alone to capture all relevant changes in brain state.
neurips-2025-evobrain-dynamic-multi-chan.tldr: EvoBrain lets EEG graph nodes and connections evolve over time, improving seizure detection over a dynamic GNN baseline.

paragraphs: HiFlow aims to generate higher-resolution images with pretrained text-to-image flow models without additional training. The paper argues that existing training-free approaches often rely too heavily on the final result of low-resolution sampling. Intermediate states also contain useful information about how image structure and detail develop, and discarding that information can contribute to artifacts or weak detail.

The method constructs a virtual reference flow in the high-resolution space using information from the low-resolution flow. It guides generation in three ways: aligning initialization to maintain broad, low-frequency consistency; aligning direction to preserve structure; and aligning acceleration to improve detail fidelity. Guidance therefore draws on the evolution of generation rather than only its endpoint.

Experiments report higher-quality high-resolution images than state-of-the-art comparison methods. The framework also works across personalized variants of the text-to-image models studied. The contribution is a training-free, model-agnostic way to use an existing flow model's sampling behavior as guidance for higher-resolution generation, with the reported gains supported by the experimental evaluations.
neurips-2025-hiflow-training-free-high-r.tldr: HiFlow uses intermediate low-resolution flow information to guide higher-quality high-resolution image generation without retraining.

paragraphs: HyPINO generates physics-informed neural networks from descriptions of partial differential equations, aiming to solve new problems without task-specific fine-tuning. Its demonstrated scope covers two-dimensional linear elliptic, hyperbolic, and parabolic equations, with varying sources, geometries, and mixed boundary conditions. A Swin Transformer hypernetwork learns from both analytically generated solutions and unlabeled examples supervised through physics-based objectives.

The method also improves a predicted solution through repeated forward passes. It treats the generated network's residual as a new corrective equation, produces another network to address that residual, and adds the solutions together. This refinement reduces error on six benchmarks, with a greater than 100-fold reduction in L2 loss in the best case.

Across seven benchmarks, HyPINO reports strong zero-shot accuracy and outperforms U-Nets, Poseidon, and PINO. When its generated networks are subsequently fine-tuned, they converge faster and reach lower final errors than random and Reptile-based initialization on five benchmarks, matching them on two. Extension to nonlinear and higher-dimensional equations is presented as future potential, beyond the demonstrated scope.
neurips-2025-hypino-multi-physics-neural.tldr: HyPINO generates physics-informed solvers for varied two-dimensional linear PDEs and refines their solutions through additional forward passes.

paragraphs: K-DeCore addresses a continual-learning task in which a model repeatedly learns to translate natural-language questions into structured queries. Each new task may involve a different body or organization of structured knowledge. General continual-learning methods can struggle to transfer reasoning across these differences, and approaches that keep adding parameters become less efficient as tasks accumulate.

The framework separates reasoning into task-specific and task-independent stages. This gives it a way to distinguish knowledge tied to a particular task from reasoning that can transfer across tasks. It combines that separation with memory consolidation tailored to the distinct stages and a method for generating synthetic training examples guided by the structure of the knowledge.

K-DeCore maintains a fixed number of tunable parameters as it handles sequential tasks. Experiments on four benchmark datasets, using multiple backbone language models, report improvements over existing continual-learning approaches across several metrics. The results support combining knowledge separation, memory consolidation, and structured synthetic data to improve transfer without continually expanding the trainable parameter set.
neurips-2025-k-decore-facilitating-knowl.tldr: K-DeCore separates shared and task-specific reasoning to improve continual structured-query learning with a fixed number of tunable parameters.

paragraphs: Equivariant networks encode the expectation that transforming an input should produce a corresponding transformation in the output. This can improve learning when the data respect those symmetries. Real data may only approximately satisfy them because of noise, structural variation, or measurement bias. The paper also notes that strict symmetry constraints can make optimization harder even when the data are fully symmetric.

Adaptive Constrained Equivariance, or ACE, starts with a flexible model that is not forced to be equivariant. During training, it gradually tightens a constraint on departures from equivariance. This follows a homotopy-inspired strategy: begin with an easier optimization problem and progressively transform it toward the desired constrained problem.

The gradual process allows the model to settle at a data-driven balance between symmetry and flexibility. Across several architectures and tasks, ACE improves performance, sample efficiency, and robustness to input perturbations relative to strictly equivariant models and heuristic relaxations. These findings support treating the strength of symmetry enforcement as part of the learning process.
neurips-2025-learning-approximately-equi.tldr: ACE gradually tightens equivariance constraints during training to balance useful symmetries with the flexibility required by data.

paragraphs: Variational inference approximates a difficult probability distribution using a more manageable family, choosing the member that minimizes Kullback-Leibler divergence. For exponential families, the optimal approximation obeys a fixed-point equation. This paper builds Least Squares Variational Inference, or LSVI, around that equation, turning each update into a familiar regression problem.

Each iteration uses Monte Carlo samples from the current approximation and performs ordinary least squares on tempered log-target evaluations. The method does not require gradients of the target. The authors show that its updates are equivalent to biased stochastic natural gradient descent, which lets them derive convergence rates in terms of sample counts and iterations.

For Gaussian approximations, the regression formulation avoids explicitly inverting a Fisher information matrix whose size grows quadratically with dimension. The resulting complexity is cubic in dimension for full covariance and linear for mean-field approximations. Numerical studies on logistic regression, discrete variable selection, and Bayesian synthetic likelihood report competitive performance with state-of-the-art methods, including settings where gradients are unavailable.
neurips-2025-least-squares-variational-i.tldr: LSVI performs gradient-free variational inference through repeated least-squares regression, with convergence analysis and efficient Gaussian updates.

paragraphs: MolFLAE creates a shared latent representation for three-dimensional molecules so that molecular editing can happen by navigating that space. The motivation is to change a molecule while retaining useful features such as shape, chemical properties, or interactions. Unlike approaches organized around separately supervised editing tasks, the proposed representation supports several kinds of manipulation without task-specific training.

The variational autoencoder maps molecules with different atom counts into a fixed number of latent nodes, distinguished by learned embeddings. Its encoder and latent space are E(3)-equivariant, preserving the relevant relationship to spatial transformations. A Bayesian Flow Network reconstructs molecular structures from the regularized latent representation.

The model achieves competitive unconditional molecule-generation performance and supports atom-count editing, reconstruction, and coordinated interpolation of structure and properties. In a human glucocorticoid receptor optimization task, it generates molecules with improved hydrophilicity while preserving key interactions under computational evaluation. That result demonstrates a computational editing application; the broader contribution is a common representation that accommodates both changing molecular size and controlled structural manipulation.
neurips-2025-manipulating-3d-molecules-i.tldr: MolFLAE supports zero-shot 3D molecule editing through a fixed-dimensional, spatially equivariant latent representation.

paragraphs: MedAgentBoard tests whether collaboration among multiple language-model agents provides practical advantages on medical tasks. It compares these systems with both single language models and established conventional methods. The motivation is that evaluations covering only a narrow task range, or omitting strong alternatives, cannot adequately establish when the additional complexity of collaboration is useful.

The benchmark covers medical question answering, including visual questions; summaries written for non-specialists; predictions from structured electronic health records; and clinical workflow automation. Its inputs span text, medical images, and structured records. This breadth allows the evaluation to examine whether an approach's benefits transfer across different forms of medical work.

The findings vary by task. Multi-agent systems improve task completeness in some workflow-automation scenarios, but do not consistently beat advanced single models in textual medical question answering. Specialized conventional methods generally perform better on medical visual question answering and record-based prediction. The results favor task-specific selection, weighing the complexity and overhead of collaboration against demonstrated performance gains.
neurips-2025-medagentboard-benchmarking-.tldr: MedAgentBoard finds that multi-agent medical AI helps in some scenarios but does not consistently outperform single models or specialized conventional methods.

paragraphs: Multi-view stereo depends on matching features accurately across images taken from different viewpoints. Recent methods use Transformers to combine local features with longer-range information, but their quadratic computational complexity makes efficiency harder to maintain. MVSMamba investigates Mamba as an alternative with global modeling capability and linear complexity.

The network's central component is a Dynamic Mamba module built around reference-centered dynamic scanning. This organizes feature interaction within images and between the reference and source views. It is designed to produce representations that incorporate multiple directions and aggregate global information at multiple scales. The scanning strategy adapts Mamba's processing to the relationships needed for multi-view matching.

Experiments on DTU and Tanks-and-Temples report better performance and efficiency than state-of-the-art multi-view stereo methods. The paper's contribution is therefore both an architectural adaptation and an empirical result: it shows how global feature aggregation using Mamba can support strong matching representations with minimal computational overhead in the evaluated multi-view stereo settings.
neurips-2025-mvsmamba-multi-view-stereo-.tldr: MVSMamba uses reference-centered dynamic scanning to improve multi-view stereo feature aggregation, performance, and efficiency.

paragraphs: Concept erasure tries to remove unwanted attributes from learned representations while retaining information useful for the intended task. The paper argues that existing methods leave nonlinear dependencies that an adversary can exploit to recover those attributes. It also asks how much useful information is lost as erasure progresses, making the changing protection-utility trade-off a central object of study.

Obliviator formulates erasure through functions and a composition of kernels. Because the resulting optimization problem lacks a closed-form solution, it gradually transforms the feature space through iterative updates. This provides a route to protection against nonlinear adversaries while tracking how the transformation affects task utility.

The reported trade-off curves outperform the baselines, indicating a better balance between attribute protection and retained usefulness. Erasure is also more utility-preserving for better-disentangled representations produced by more capable models. That finding links the cost of removing an attribute to how information is organized in the starting representation, while the iterative approach exposes how this cost develops during erasure.
neurips-2025-obliviator-reveals-the-cost.tldr: Obliviator iteratively erases nonlinear attribute information while measuring and improving the trade-off between protection and task utility.

paragraphs: Bayesian optimization searches for good solutions when evaluating an objective is expensive and gradients may be unavailable. This paper targets the short planning horizon of methods that emphasize the next evaluation. Such one-step decisions can favor local optima and perform poorly on complex or high-dimensional problems, motivating a search strategy that considers several steps ahead.

REBMBO combines a Gaussian process for local guidance with an energy-based model for broader structural information. It frames each optimization iteration as a Markov decision process and uses Proximal Policy Optimization to choose adaptive multi-step exploration. The planning mechanism adjusts both how deeply to look ahead and which directions to explore.

Experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks report superior performance, while additional tests with different Gaussian-process configurations support adaptability and robustness. The approach's significance lies in joining local predictions, global structure, and learned sequential planning within one optimizer. The reported evidence supports this combination on the evaluated problems, without implying that multi-step search always avoids local optima.
neurips-2025-optimizing-the-unknown-blac.tldr: REBMBO combines Gaussian processes, an energy-based model, and reinforcement learning for adaptive multi-step black-box optimization.

paragraphs: This paper introduces purification: converting an approximately differentially private mechanism into a purely differentially private one under certain conditions. Approximate privacy uses epsilon and delta parameters, while the purified mechanism has delta equal to zero and potentially a different epsilon. The conversion uses randomized post-processing with calibrated noise to obtain a near-optimal privacy-utility trade-off for pure privacy.

The framework suggests designing a suitable approximate-private algorithm first, then purifying its output. This makes it possible to build pure-private methods using techniques such as strong composition and propose-test-release that require a positive delta during their usual design. The conditional nature of the reduction matters: the abstract does not claim that every approximate-private mechanism can be converted this way.

Applications include private empirical risk minimization, stability-based release, and query release. The authors describe the reduction as the first statistically and computationally efficient one of its kind, to their knowledge. They also use it to derive approximate-privacy lower bounds with explicit delta dependence, avoiding sophisticated fingerprinting-code constructions.
neurips-2025-purifying-approximate-diffe.tldr: Under certain conditions, randomized post-processing converts approximate differential privacy into pure privacy with a near-optimal privacy-utility trade-off.

paragraphs: Safe and Stable Diffusion, or S²Diff, brings explicit safety and stability considerations into diffusion-based control. The paper observes that policies focused on maximizing reward or minimizing cost can overlook these requirements. Its model-based framework uses a Lyapunov perspective, connecting control decisions to learned certificate functions that support reasoning about safety and stability.

The authors show how to obtain globally valid control policies driven by these certificates without relying on complex gradient-based optimization solvers or a control-affine system structure. They also establish connections between diffusion sampling and almost Lyapunov theory. These connections allow policies operating over trajectories to help learn better certificate functions, linking policy generation and certificate learning.

Experiments across varied dynamical systems report consistent improvements over certificate-based controllers and model-based diffusion baselines in safety, stability, and overall control performance. The contribution combines a theoretical connection with a practical control framework: learned certificates guide diffusion policies, while trajectory-level policies contribute to improving the certificates used for the safety and stability guarantees.
neurips-2025-safe-and-stable-control-via.tldr: S²Diff connects diffusion control with learned Lyapunov certificates to improve safety, stability, and control performance.

paragraphs: This paper examines how unequal token frequencies affect optimization in a linear bigram model for next-token prediction. Token probabilities follow a power law controlled by an exponent, including the Zipf-like case where frequency is inversely proportional to rank. This simplified setting helps isolate how the data distribution changes the difficulty of training.

The authors derive iteration-scaling laws for deterministic gradient descent and sign descent, using the latter as a proxy for Adam. Their analysis includes heavier-tailed distributions than those emphasized in earlier theory. When probability mass is less concentrated among a few components, the optimization problem becomes harder because a small set of dominant components accounts for less of the loss.

Within this setting, the Zipf case is worst-case for gradient descent: reaching a small relative error requires an iteration count that grows almost linearly with dimension. Sign descent needs iterations growing only with the square root of dimension in that case. The result provides a theoretical explanation for a substantial optimizer advantage at large vocabulary sizes in the studied model.
neurips-2025-scaling-laws-for-gradient-d.tldr: For a linear bigram model with Zipf-distributed tokens, sign descent has substantially better dimension-dependent iteration scaling than gradient descent.

paragraphs: This paper investigates how to infer connections between neurons from their recorded activity. The task is difficult because some neurons are unobserved and the inference model may not match the circuit's true dynamics. The proposed approach represents neurons as interacting graph nodes and learns connectivity while also predicting future spikes.

The architecture separates structural learning from activity prediction into two modules. One learns the latent connections; the other uses a graph neural network to predict subsequent neural activity. Auxiliary nodes account for neurons that are not directly observed. The spike-prediction task supplies self-supervision that links a proposed network structure to its ability to explain evolving activity.

Tests use simulated ring-attractor networks and recordings from mouse head-direction cells. Across changes in recurrent connectivity, external inputs, and observation completeness, the model resolves spurious correlations and recovers accurate weight profiles. For real recordings, inferred connectivity agrees with continuous-attractor theory. These findings support the potential of prediction-driven graph learning to reveal latent circuitry under partial observation.
neurips-2025-self-supervised-discovery-o.tldr: A graph model learns hidden neural connectivity through spike prediction, using auxiliary nodes to account for unobserved neurons.

paragraphs: SSDiff restores faces in old photographs affected by combinations of scratches, breakage, fading, and severe blur. Such damage can be highly localized, making global guidance poorly suited to deciding which facial regions need repair. The paper also identifies natural face color as a challenge for existing diffusion-guided restoration methods.

A pretrained diffusion model first generates pseudo-reference faces under weak guidance. Their aligned contours and natural colors provide supervision for restoration. Structural guidance operates throughout denoising, while color refinement is introduced later, matching diffusion's coarse-to-fine progression. Face-parsing maps and scratch masks direct the restoration toward damaged regions, with the aim of avoiding identity mismatch.

The authors also introduce VintageFace, a benchmark containing 300 real old face photographs with different degradation levels. They report improvements over GAN-based and diffusion-based methods in perceptual quality, fidelity, and regional controllability. The central contribution is to combine generated reference information with selective, staged guidance, allowing structure, color, and localized damage to receive different treatment during restoration.
neurips-2025-self-supervised-selective-g.tldr: SSDiff uses generated face references and region-specific, staged diffusion guidance to restore damaged old photographs.

paragraphs: TANDEM addresses how to choose the proportions of different data domains when training a language model. The mixture matters because domains can contribute differently to model capability. The paper frames choosing those proportions as a bi-level optimization problem, in which decisions about the data mixture are tied to the model training they produce.

The authors simplify that formulation into a single-level problem with a penalty and solve it using two networks. A proxy model trains on primary data, while a dynamically updated reference model trains with additional data. Differences between the models estimate how effective the extra data is, and TANDEM increases the weight of domains that benefit more from it.

The method comes with theoretical guarantees and is evaluated across multiple settings. The bi-level perspective also motivates studying mixture optimization when data are restricted and during supervised fine-tuning. Experiments report significant performance improvements from optimized ratios in these settings. The contribution is an adaptive way to allocate training emphasis using observed benefit from additional data.
neurips-2025-tandem-bi-level-data-mixtur.tldr: TANDEM compares twin training networks to increase the weight of data domains that benefit more from additional examples.

paragraphs: The Latent Denoising Diffusion Bridge Model, or LDDBM, translates information between modalities through a shared latent representation. Existing translation approaches can impose restrictions such as matching input and output dimensions, Gaussian source priors, or specialized architectures. This paper seeks a more general framework by extending diffusion bridges with latent variables.

The shared latent space lets the method connect modalities without requiring their original dimensions to align. A contrastive loss encourages paired examples to retain consistent meaning, while a predictive loss guides accurate translation into the target domain. A domain-agnostic encoder-decoder architecture handles latent-space noise prediction, and the authors explore training strategies intended to improve stability.

Evaluations cover multi-view-to-3D shape generation, image super-resolution, and multi-view scene synthesis. Experiments and ablations report strong performance and support the effectiveness of the framework's components. The contribution is a common translation approach that combines latent bridging with semantic alignment and predictive supervision, reducing dependence on modality-specific architectural choices across the tasks studied.
neurips-2025-towards-general-modality-tr.tldr: LDDBM combines latent diffusion bridges with contrastive and predictive losses to translate between modalities without matching their original dimensions.

paragraphs: This paper tackles the difficulty of making dense language-model layers understandable without substantially changing their behavior. Sparse approximations can expose specialized features, but inaccurate reconstruction can increase next-token prediction loss. The authors propose shifting sparsity from individual neurons to specialized sublayers, giving each active component greater expressive capacity.

Mixture of Decoders, or MxDs, expands pretrained dense layers into tens of thousands of sparsely activated sublayers. A flexible tensor factorization lets each sublayer implement a linear transformation with full-rank weights. This design preserves expressive capacity even under heavy sparsity and generalizes multilayer perceptrons and gated linear units.

Experiments on language models with up to three billion parameters show a better sparsity-accuracy trade-off than methods including Transcoders. Sparse probing and feature-steering evaluations find similarly specialized natural-language features. The findings suggest that layer-level sparsity can improve the faithfulness of interpretable decompositions while retaining useful specialization. They establish an improved trade-off in the evaluated models, rather than complete interpretability of every component.
neurips-2025-towards-interpretability-wi.tldr: Mixture of Decoders uses sparse, expressive sublayers to improve the accuracy of interpretable language-model layer decompositions.

paragraphs: UniCTokens connects understanding and image generation for user-provided concepts. Separate concept tokens can leave these tasks disconnected: a system may need to generate a known subject with its associated hat even when the prompt does not describe that hat. The paper calls this personalized knowledge-driven generation, where producing the image depends on previously learned concept knowledge.

The framework trains shared concept tokens inside a unified vision-language model. Training progresses through understanding warm-up, using understanding to bootstrap generation, and then using generation to deepen understanding. The shared representation and staged process are intended to let the two tasks benefit from complementary information.

The authors introduce UnifyBench to evaluate concept understanding, concept generation, and knowledge-driven generation together. Results show competitive performance on the first two and state-of-the-art performance on personalized knowledge-driven generation. The reported findings support reciprocal benefits: stronger understanding helps generation, while the generation process contributes useful information to understanding. The contribution combines a shared personalization mechanism with an evaluation framework for these connected capabilities.
neurips-2025-unictokens-boosting-persona.tldr: UniCTokens shares concept tokens across personalized understanding and generation, improving image generation that depends on learned personal knowledge.

paragraphs: This paper develops variational inference using equally weighted mixtures of isotropic Gaussian distributions. Each component has a covariance proportional to the identity, so its spread is the same in every direction. Combining several such components offers a way to approximate a posterior with multiple modes while keeping each individual component simple.

The motivation is a balance between representational flexibility and computational cost. Gaussian mixtures with general covariance matrices allow more elaborate component shapes, but require more memory and computation. The chosen family retains multiple adjustable centers and variance parameters without giving every component a full covariance structure. The authors develop a variational framework and algorithms specifically for this family.

Their algorithms use gradient descent to update component locations and either entropic mirror descent or Bures descent to update variances. Numerical experiments illustrate performance. The contribution is an efficient optimization approach for this particular approximation family, aimed at capturing multimodal Bayesian posteriors through mixtures of simple components rather than increasing the complexity of each component.
neurips-2025-variational-inference-with-.tldr: The paper develops efficient variational-inference algorithms using equally weighted isotropic Gaussian mixtures to approximate multimodal posteriors.
